codeReview.summary: The implementation correctly replaces host-OS behavioral monitoring (PowerShell/wmic subprocess calls) with Docker-based isolated execution. A new DockerSandbox class in docker_sandbox.py builds a prepared image (reveng-python:3.11-slim-strace) from python:3.11-slim with strace installed, then runs binaries inside containers with --rm --network=none and captures strace -f -e trace=network,file,process output. BehavioralMonitor.start_monitoring() now delegates to DockerSandbox in its worker thread, parses strace syscalls into BehaviorEvent objects, preserves ML anomaly scoring, and the SKIP_SANDBOX env var returns a static-only profile with sandbox_available=false. The pipeline_engine.py correctly surfaces sandbox_available and analysis_mode. Four well-structured unit tests cover the core scenarios with proper mocking.

issues.description: Legacy _monitor_file_operations, _monitor_registry_operations, _monitor_network_operations, _monitor_process_operations, _monitor_memory_operations, _monitor_system_operations, _monitor_crypto_operations, and _monitor_anti_analysis methods (lines 468-773) remain in the file. They contain subprocess.run calls to 'powershell', 'reg query', 'netstat', 'wmic', etc. These methods are now dead code — unreachable from the new _monitor_behavior() implementation — but they add ~300 lines of unused code with host-OS commands. Should be removed or clearly marked as deprecated in a cleanup pass.

The sandbox metadata field assignments on the BehavioralProfile constructor (lines 900-908) use long ternary expressions. While functionally correct, extracting these into a helper method would improve readability.

The timeout is capped at 30 seconds (max(1, min(int(timeout_seconds or self.timeout_seconds), 30))). While this matches the spec, it means callers passing duration > 30 will silently have it capped. Consider logging when the timeout is reduced.

summary: PASS. The docker-sandbox feature is well-implemented. DockerSandbox correctly isolates binary execution in python:3.11-slim containers with strace tracing, BehavioralMonitor.start_monitoring() properly delegates to the sandbox instead of host-process enumeration, containers are cleaned up after stop_monitoring(), and SKIP_SANDBOX returns graceful static-only results. All 4 expected behaviors are satisfied. The only notable issue is ~300 lines of dead legacy _monitor_* methods (with powershell/wmic calls) that remain in the file but are unreachable from the new code path — this is non-blocking dead code that should be cleaned up in a future pass.
